implementationPlan.description: THE BOUNDED PROJECTION — NEW `apps/daemon/src/deployment/migration-observation.ts` plus its one-line `.js` bridge, with a NAME-MATCHED `migration-observation.test.ts` in step 3. IT IS THE ONE PLACE a durable migration receipt becomes a safe, bounded, exposable fact, so both read boundaries share one decoder and one safety rule. INPUT: a project id and a DEPLOY RECEIPT already on the environment row. RESOLUTION IS A DURABLE KEY LOOKUP, NEVER A SEARCH: the deploy receipt's `decisionId` IS the migration `requestId`, so call `readMigrationReceipt(store, projectId, deployReceipt.decisionId)`. DO NOT enumerate `migration:` aggregates, and DO NOT select by filename, SHA, latest timestamp or arbitrary requestId — DoD 2 forbids exactly those. REUSE THE STRICT EXISTING DECODER: `readMigrationReceipt` already throws `MIGRATION_RECEIPT_INVALID` on a corrupt or unverifiable record; catch it and answer UNKNOWN-with-that-code, never APPLIED and never "no pending work". THREE DISTINCT ANSWERS, and the distinction is the point: NO receipt found (the deploy composed no migration — `ports.migrate` is optional, deploy-ports.ts:94) is UNKNOWN; a corrupt/unverifiable receipt is UNKNOWN carrying the decoder's code AND layer; a decoded receipt is a known observation. EXPOSE, all bounded: environment, receiptId, outcome (APPLIED | REFUSED | REVERTED), the applied/reverted identifiers, a nullable backup reference, and for a refusal its code, its layer and the FAILING FILE BASENAME ONLY. LABEL IT A PROJECT/ENVIRONMENT OBSERVATION — the receipt has no goalRef/nodeRef (eleven keys, migration-receipt.ts:22-36) and must never be presented as node or goal ownership (task rail 3). SAFETY IS ENFORCED HERE, ONCE: re-validate each applied entry with the existing `migrationFilename` guard rather than forwarding raw; bound the refusal detail to a basename; never emit a database URL, password, SQL, full diagnostic output, credential hash or prefix, or an untrusted path (DoD 4). The backup reference is a NON-DOWNLOAD reference with a hash only when verified as an existing confined backup; a missing backup reads missing, never present, and REFUSED may legitimately carry null. DO NOT change the eleven-key persisted receipt (task rail 2). Keep the module under 250 lines.

RESOLUTION IS A DURABLE KEY LOOKUP. `readMigrationObservation(store, projectId, environment, deployReceipt, options)` calls `readMigrationReceipt(store, projectId, deployReceipt.decisionId)` and nothing else. No aggregate enumeration, no filename/sha/timestamp/arbitrary-requestId selection anywhere in the module.

THREE DISTINCT ANSWERS. `deployReceipt === null` or no receipt at the key -> UNKNOWN/`MIGRATION_RECEIPT_ABSENT`. Corrupt or unverifiable -> UNKNOWN/`MIGRATION_RECEIPT_INVALID` with layer `DAEMON_INGRESS` (caught from the strict existing decoder's throw). Decoded -> OBSERVED. `migrations` is NULL while UNKNOWN and an array only when OBSERVED, so an empty list can only ever mean known-none.

SERVED SHAPE — FLAT ON PURPOSE (13 members): subject, environment, state, receiptId, outcome, migrations, backupState, backupSha256, refusalCode, refusalLayer, refusalFile, unknownCode, unknownLayer. Flat so the browser can pin one exact-key roster in a single pass with no nested optional records to widen a member at a time. `subject` is the constant `PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` — DoD 2 / task rail 3: the receipt's eleven keys carry no nodeRef or goalRef, so project+environment is the only honest attribution.

SAFETY, ENFORCED ONCE HERE.
- `applied[]`: re-validated with the production `migrationFilename` guard. If ANY entry fails, the whole observation fails closed to UNKNOWN rather than being served with the bad entry silently dropped.
- `refusalFile`: `migrationFilename(detail) ? detail : null`. This is load-bearing, not belt-and-braces — step 1 measured `MIGRATION_DOWN_BATCH_UNKNOWN` writing `input.toMigrationRequestId` VERBATIM into detail (migration-down-service.ts:129), caller-supplied text up to 4096 chars. Non-filename details are WITHHELD ENTIRELY, never truncated.
- `backupRef`: parsed by `/^(?<path>.+\.sql)@sha256:(?<digest>[a-f0-9]{64})$/u`. THE PATH NEVER LEAVES THE MODULE. VERIFIED requires all four of: reference parses; leaf matches `^\d{17}\.sql$`; the path equals `join(realpath(root), .moe-next, backups, pre-migration, <environment>, <leaf>)`; and `lstatSync` finds a real non-symlink file there now. Anything else is UNVERIFIED with `backupSha256: null`. `backupRef === null` is `NONE`. So a missing or unconfirmable backup can never read as present, and REFUSED may legitimately carry NONE.

TWO DESIGN CALLS, both recorded in the module doc.
(1) THE ENVIRONMENT CHECK IS A GUARD, NOT A MATCH. The key lookup has already selected the receipt; `receipt.environment !== environment` then fails closed to UNKNOWN. It never searches for an environment's receipt — it only refuses to place a selected one on a row it disagrees with. That is what the step-7 isolation drill will red.
(2) IT DOES NOT CHASE A LATER REVERT, and this is a real limit worth a grader's attention. A REVERTED receipt records NO durable link back to the batch it undid — `migration-down-service.ts` baseReceipt keeps the source's `sha` but not its `requestId` — so reaching a revert from an APPLIED receipt would need a sha or timestamp match, precisely what DoD 2 forbids. The projection therefore reports the receipt AT THE KEY. REVERTED is rendered whenever the receipt at that key is REVERTED.

NO ROOT REACHES THE READ BOUNDARY (measured at step 1), so `backupRoot` is an OPTIONAL option; absent root means no confinement proof, which means UNVERIFIED. Honest by construction: it degrades the claim, never the safety.

ALSO: exported `MIGRATION_RECEIPT_COMMAND_KIND` from `migration-receipt.ts` (module-private `const kind` before) so step 4 can import the constant instead of retyping the literal. Added export only — the eleven-key persisted receipt, its decoder and every write path are byte-unchanged (`const kind: string = MIGRATION_RECEIPT_COMMAND_KIND` keeps every existing use identical).
